items.name: Terminal
items.doc:
Terminal utilities for semantic terminal formatting and control.  
  
## What this namespace provides  
  
- Nested color and attribute enums  
- Composable text styles  
- Screen and cursor helpers  
- File-descriptor terminal capability checks  
  
## What it does not provide  
  
- Raw mode  
- Alternate screen buffers  
- Keyboard or mouse event handling  
- High-level TUI widgets or layout primitives

items.name: Cursor
items.doc:
Cursor control helpers.  
  
All cursor coordinates in this namespace are **one-based**.  
Row `1`, column `1` is the top-left corner.

items.name: hide
items.doc:
Hides the cursor.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
let hide: String = Terminal::Cursor::hide();  
```

items.name: moveTo
items.signature: function moveTo(row: u32, column: u32): String
items.doc:
Moves the cursor to one-based row and column coordinates.  
  
# Arguments  
  
- `row`: one-based terminal row.  
- `column`: one-based terminal column.  
  
# Returns  
  
A complete CSI sequence such as `ESC[12;34H`.  
  
# Invariants  
  
The function preserves the provided numeric values exactly; it does not  
clamp zero or out-of-range coordinates.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
let moveCursor: String = Terminal::Cursor::moveTo(3, 10);  
```

items.name: restore
items.doc:
Restores the most recently saved cursor position.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
let restore: String = Terminal::Cursor::restore();  
```

items.name: save
items.doc:
Saves the current cursor position.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
let save: String = Terminal::Cursor::save();  
```

items.name: show
items.doc:
Shows the cursor.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
let show: String = Terminal::Cursor::show();  
```

items.name: Screen
items.doc:
Screen control helpers.  
  
Use these methods when a caller needs a complete command string for common  
clearing operations without depending on raw ANSI fragments.

items.name: clear
items.doc:
Returns the full-screen clear command.  
  
# Returns  
  
A complete CSI sequence equivalent to ANSI `ESC[2J`.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
let clear: String = Terminal::Screen::clear();  
```

items.name: clearLine
items.doc:
Returns the current-line clear command.  
  
# Returns  
  
A complete CSI sequence equivalent to ANSI `ESC[2K`.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
let clearLine: String = Terminal::Screen::clearLine();  
```

items.name: Style
items.doc:
Composable text styling state.  
  
`Style` collects semantic foreground, background, and attribute choices  
and converts them into a single rendered string when `apply()` is called.  
  
## Rendering model  
  
```text  
  foreground? -> background? -> attributes* -> text -> reset  
```  
  
## Key behavior  
  
- Missing foreground/background means "leave terminal default unchanged"  
  until the final reset.  
- Attributes are emitted in insertion order.  
- `apply()` always appends `Terminal::reset()`.

members.name: foregroundColor
members.doc: Optional foreground color to emit before text.

members.name: backgroundColor
members.doc: Optional background color to emit before text.

members.name: attributes
members.doc: Ordered text attributes to emit before text.

members.name: new
members.doc:
Creates an empty style with no colors or attributes.  
  
# Returns  
  
A style that leaves all formatting unset until additional builder-style  
methods are called.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
let style: Terminal::Style = Terminal::Style::new();  
```

members.name: apply
members.doc:
Applies the style to `text` and appends a trailing reset.  
  
# Arguments  
  
- `text`: text payload to wrap.  
  
# Returns  
  
An owned `String` containing all configured prefix sequences, then the  
original text, then `Terminal::reset()`.  
  
# Invariants  
  
- Always returns a trailing reset.  
- Never mutates the input text.  
- Attribute order matches insertion order.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
let mut style: Terminal::Style = Terminal::Style::new();  
style.foreground(Terminal::TerminalColor::RED);  
let styled: String = style.apply("alert");  
```

members.name: attribute
members.doc:
Appends one text attribute to the style.  
  
# Arguments  
  
- `attribute`: attribute to emit before the text.  
  
# Notes  
  
Repeated calls preserve insertion order. The module does not currently  
deduplicate attributes or validate conflicting combinations.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
let mut style: Terminal::Style = Terminal::Style::new();  
style.attribute(Terminal::TerminalAttribute::BOLD);  
style.attribute(Terminal::TerminalAttribute::UNDERLINE);  
```

members.name: background
members.doc:
Sets the style background color.  
  
# Arguments  
  
- `color`: semantic background color to use for later `apply()` calls.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
let mut style: Terminal::Style = Terminal::Style::new();  
style.background(Terminal::TerminalColor::BLUE);  
```

members.name: foreground
members.doc:
Sets the style foreground color.  
  
# Arguments  
  
- `color`: semantic color to use for later `apply()` calls.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
let mut style: Terminal::Style = Terminal::Style::new();  
style.foreground(Terminal::TerminalColor::GREEN);  
```

items.name: TerminalAttribute
items.doc:
Text attributes represented by ANSI SGR codes.  
  
Combine one or more of these through `Terminal::Style::attribute()`.

members.name: code

items.name: TerminalColor
items.doc:
ANSI 8-color palette used by semantic styling helpers.  
  
These values describe **intent** rather than literal bytes. Convert them  
to concrete escape codes through `foregroundCode()` or `backgroundCode()`.  
Most callers should use them through `Terminal::Style`, `colorText`, or  
`styledText` instead of calling the code helpers themselves.

members.name: backgroundCode
members.doc:
Returns the ANSI background SGR code for this color.  
  
# Returns  
  
One of the standard background codes in the 40–49 range.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
let code: i32 = Terminal::TerminalColor::BLUE.backgroundCode();  
// code == 44  
```

members.name: foregroundCode
members.doc:
Returns the ANSI foreground SGR code for this color.  
  
# Returns  
  
One of the standard foreground codes in the 30–39 range.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
let code: i32 = Terminal::TerminalColor::RED.foregroundCode();  
// code == 31  
```

items.name: appendStyled
items.signature: function appendStyled(output: &mut String, text: str, useAnsi: boolean, color: TerminalColor, bold: boolean): void
items.doc: Appends optionally styled text to `output`.

items.name: colorText
items.signature: function colorText(text: str, color: TerminalColor): String
items.doc:
Wraps text in one foreground color and a trailing reset.  
  
# Arguments  
  
- `text`: text payload to wrap.  
- `color`: semantic foreground color.  
  
# Returns  
  
Styled text equivalent to constructing a new `Style`, setting its  
foreground color, and calling `apply(text)`.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
let ok: String = Terminal::colorText("ok", Terminal::TerminalColor::GREEN);  
```

items.name: isErrorTerminal
items.doc:
Returns `true` when stderr is attached to a terminal.  
  
This is useful for tooling that styles diagnostics separately from normal  
stdout output.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
let canStyleErrors: boolean = Terminal::isErrorTerminal();  
```

items.name: isInputTerminal
items.doc:
Returns `true` when stdin is attached to a terminal.  
  
# Returns  
  
Host `isatty(STDIN_FILENO) != 0` on supported platforms.  
  
# Limitations  
  
This check is only available on the hosts enabled by the surrounding  
`@configFlag` annotation.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
let interactive: boolean = Terminal::isInputTerminal();  
```

items.name: isOutputTerminal
reset
items.doc:
Resets color and style attributes.  
  
# Returns  
  
The complete ANSI reset sequence `ESC[0m`.  
  
# Notes  
  
`Style::apply`, `colorText`, and `styledText` all append this sequence  
automatically, so callers rarely need to concatenate it manually.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
let reset: String = Terminal::reset();  
```

items.name: stripAnsiAndWhitespace
items.doc:
Strips ANSI escape sequences and ASCII whitespace from rendered text.  
  
This is intended for tests and compatibility comparisons where diagnostic  
styling and layout whitespace should not affect semantic equality.

items.name: styledIf
items.signature: function styledIf(text: str, useAnsi: boolean, color: TerminalColor, bold: boolean): String
items.doc:
Applies optional ANSI styling to `text`.  
  
When `useAnsi` is false, this returns `text` unchanged as an owned string.  
When `useAnsi` is true, it applies the requested foreground color and  
optional bold attribute with a trailing reset.

items.name: styledText
items.signature: function styledText(text: str, attribute: TerminalAttribute): String
items.doc:
Wraps text in one text attribute and a trailing reset.  
  
# Arguments  
  
- `text`: text payload to wrap.  
- `attribute`: semantic attribute to apply.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
let heading: String = Terminal::styledText("Title", Terminal::TerminalAttribute::BOLD);  
```

items.name: ansiCsi
items.doc:
Builds a Control Sequence Introducer (CSI) escape sequence.  
  
# Purpose  
  
This is a private implementation helper used by the public semantic API.  
Callers should prefer `Terminal::Style`, `Terminal::Screen`, and  
`Terminal::Cursor` instead of assembling CSI commands directly.  
  
# Arguments  
  
- `command`: trailing CSI payload such as `"2J"`, `"12;34H"`, or `"0m"`.  
  
# Returns  
  
An owned `String` beginning with `ESC [` followed by `command`.  
  
# Invariants  
  
- Always returns a complete CSI prefix.  
- Does not append any trailing reset or newline on its own.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
let sequence: String = ansiCsi("2J");  
// sequence is ESC[2J  
```

items.name: ansiSgr
items.doc:
Builds one Select Graphic Rendition (SGR) command.  
  
# Purpose  
  
Converts one numeric SGR code into a full CSI escape string. This helper is  
private so the public API can remain semantic.  
  
# Arguments  
  
- `code`: ANSI SGR code such as `0`, `31`, or `1`.  
  
# Returns  
  
A complete ANSI sequence like `ESC[31m`.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
let red: String = ansiSgr(31);  
// red is ESC[31m  
```

items.name: Test
items.doc:
Assertion and snapshot helpers for `@test` bodies.  
  
`Test` is a pure namespace surface used by the native `ignis test` runner.  
It does not hold state; instead, snapshot helpers read runner-provided  
environment variables to discover the active test name, snapshot directory,  
and update mode.  
  
Equality assertions route through canonical builtin `@eq<T>` dispatch.  
Snapshot assertions compare or update UTF-8 text files in a sibling  
`__snapshots__/` directory.

items.name: assert
assertEq
items.signature: function assertEq<T>(left: T, right: T): void
items.doc:
Fails the current test when two values are not equal under canonical `Eq`.  
  
`T` must be supported by builtin `@eq<T>`. For user-defined records and  
enums this means implementing canonical `std::hash::Eq` with a valid  
`equals(&self, other: &T): boolean` method.  
  
# Type Parameters  
  
* `T` - The type being compared.  
  
# Arguments  
  
* `left` - Left-hand value.  
* `right` - Right-hand value.  
  
# Panics  
  
Panics with `"assertion failed: values are not equal"` when the values do  
not compare equal.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
import Test from "std::test";  
  
@test  
function compareNumbers(): void {  
  Test::assertEq<i32>(40 + 2, 42);  
  Test::assertEq<str>("abc", "abc");  
}  
```

items.name: assertFileSnapshot
items.signature: function assertFileSnapshot(name: str, filePath: str): void
items.doc:
Reads `filePath` as UTF-8 text before applying snapshot comparison.  
  
This is useful when the code under test writes an artifact to disk and the  
test wants the snapshot baseline to track the file contents.  
  
# Arguments  
  
* `name` - Logical snapshot label within the current test.  
* `filePath` - Path to a UTF-8 text file to snapshot.  
  
# Panics  
  
Panics with `"snapshot assertion failed"` if the input file cannot be  
read, if the snapshot mismatches without update mode, or if snapshot I/O  
fails.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
import Test from "std::test";  
  
@test  
function snapshotFile(): void {  
  Test::assertFileSnapshot("artifact", "./actual-output.txt");  
}  
```

items.name: assertNe
items.signature: function assertNe<T>(left: T, right: T): void
items.doc:
Fails the current test when two values are equal under canonical `Eq`.  
  
This is the inverse of `assertEq<T>`.  
  
# Type Parameters  
  
* `T` - The type being compared.  
  
# Arguments  
  
* `left` - Left-hand value.  
* `right` - Right-hand value.  
  
# Panics  
  
Panics with `"assertion failed: values are equal"` when the values compare  
equal.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
import Test from "std::test";  
  
@test  
function compareDifferentValues(): void {  
  Test::assertNe<i32>(1, 2);  
}  
```

items.name: assertSnapshot
items.signature: function assertSnapshot(name: str, actual: str): void
items.doc:
Fails the current test when the named text snapshot does not match.  
  
The snapshot file is resolved from the current test name and the snapshot  
label, then stored in a sibling `__snapshots__/` directory next to the  
module under test.  
  
# Arguments  
  
* `name` - Logical snapshot label within the current test.  
* `actual` - UTF-8 text to compare or write.  
  
# Update Mode  
  
When `ignis test --update-snapshots` is active, missing or mismatched  
snapshots are written to disk instead of failing the test.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
import Test from "std::test";  
  
@test  
function snapshotText(): void {  
  Test::assertSnapshot("rendered", "hello snapshot\n");  
}  
```

items.name: fail
assertSnapshotText
items.doc:
Internal text snapshot engine shared by `Test::assertSnapshot` and  
`Test::assertFileSnapshot`.  
  
This resolves runner context, computes the snapshot file path, performs  
compare-or-update behavior, and emits bounded mismatch diagnostics before  
panicking on failure.

items.name: escapeSnapshotComponent
items.doc:
Escapes a file-name component into a deterministic ASCII-safe string.  
  
Safe bytes are kept as-is. All other bytes are rewritten as  
`_<hex><hex>`.  
  
# Arguments  
  
* `value` - Raw component to normalize for use in a file name.

items.name: failSnapshotIo
items.signature: function failSnapshotIo(reason: str, snapshotPath: str, detail: str): void
items.doc:
Emits a standard snapshot I/O diagnostic and panics.  
  
# Arguments  
  
* `reason` - High-level failure category.  
* `snapshotPath` - Path associated with the failed I/O operation.  
* `detail` - Small detail string included in stderr output.

items.name: failSnapshotMismatch
items.signature: function failSnapshotMismatch(snapshotPath: &String, expectedBytes: u64, actualBytes: u64): void
items.doc:
Emits a standard mismatch diagnostic and panics.  
  
The byte counts are reported to keep diagnostics stable and compact even  
for large snapshot bodies.  
  
# Arguments  
  
* `snapshotPath` - Snapshot file path.  
* `expectedBytes` - Byte length of the baseline snapshot.  
* `actualBytes` - Byte length of the actual snapshot text.

items.name: failSnapshotMissing
items.doc:
Emits a standard `snapshot missing` failure and panics.  
  
# Arguments  
  
* `snapshotPath` - Missing snapshot file path.

items.name: hexDigit
items.doc: Converts a nibble (`0..=15`) to its lowercase hexadecimal digit.

items.name: isSafeSnapshotByte
items.doc:
Returns whether a byte may appear unchanged in a snapshot file name.  
  
Safe bytes are limited to ASCII letters, digits, `-`, `.`, and `_`.

items.name: printSnapshotPath
items.doc:
Prints the normalized `snapshot: ...` line shared by all snapshot failure  
diagnostics.  
  
# Arguments  
  
* `snapshotPath` - Snapshot path to print in user-facing diagnostics.

items.name: requiredSnapshotEnv
items.doc:
Reads a required test-runner environment variable as an owned `String`.  
  
# Arguments  
  
* `name` - Name of the environment variable to read.  
  
# Panics  
  
Panics with `"snapshot assertion failed"` if the runner did not provide  
the required snapshot context variable.

items.name: snapshotFileName
items.doc:
Produces the deterministic on-disk file name for a snapshot.  
  
The file name layout is:  
  
```text  
<escaped-test-name>__<escaped-snapshot-name>.snap.txt  
```  
  
Escaping prevents collisions with path separators, `::`, spaces, and  
other punctuation while keeping ASCII-safe names for the filesystem.  
  
# Arguments  
  
* `testName` - Fully-qualified test name.  
* `snapshotName` - Logical snapshot label.

items.name: snapshotPath
items.signature: function snapshotPath(snapshotDir: &String, testName: &String, snapshotName: str): PathBuf
items.doc:
Builds the final snapshot path for the current test and snapshot label.  
  
The resulting file lives in the test's snapshot directory and uses the  
escaped file name returned by `snapshotFileName(...)`.  
  
# Arguments  
  
* `snapshotDir` - Snapshot directory provided by the runner.  
* `testName` - Fully-qualified test name.  
* `snapshotName` - Logical snapshot label within the test.

items.name: snapshotUpdateModeEnabled
items.doc:
Returns whether snapshot update mode is enabled for the current test run.  
  
The native runner encodes this as `IGNIS_TEST_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1`.

items.name: writeSnapshot
items.doc:
Writes snapshot text to disk, creating the snapshot directory first.  
  
# Arguments  
  
* `snapshotDir` - Parent snapshot directory.  
* `snapshotPath` - Full path to the snapshot file.  
* `actual` - Snapshot contents to write.  
  
# Panics  
  
Panics with `"snapshot assertion failed"` if directory creation or file  
writing fails, or if the write reports a short write.

items.name: Text
items.doc: UTF-8 to UTF-16 position conversion for editor protocols.

items.name: LineIndex
items.doc:
Line start table over an owned source text, for converting UTF-8 byte  
offsets to `Position` values and back.  
  
Building the index is one pass over the bytes. `position` finds the  
line with a binary search and then walks only that line.

members.name: lineStarts
members.doc: Byte offset of the start of each line. Never empty: line 0 starts at 0.

members.name: text
members.doc: The indexed source text.

members.name: create
members.doc: Indexes `text`, taking ownership of it.

members.name: endPosition
members.doc:
Returns the position of the end of the text: after a trailing `\n`  
that is column 0 of the empty last line.

members.name: lineCount
members.doc:
Returns the number of lines. A text ending in `\n` has an empty last  
line after it, and an empty text has one line.

members.name: lineOf
members.doc:
Returns the 0-based line that contains byte `offset`. Offsets past the  
end belong to the last line.

members.name: lineStart
members.doc: Returns the byte offset where `line` starts, or `NONE` past the last line.

members.name: offset
members.doc:
Converts a line and UTF-16 column to a UTF-8 byte offset.  
  
A line past the last one returns the text length. A column past the  
end of its line walks through the line break, so it lands on the  
start of the next line. A column inside a surrogate pair lands after  
that character.

members.name: position
members.doc:
Converts a UTF-8 byte offset to a line and UTF-16 column.  
  
An offset inside a multi-byte character reports the column of that  
character's first byte, and an offset past the end of the text reports  
the end of the text.

items.name: Position
items.doc:
A 0-based line and a 0-based column counted in UTF-16 code units, the  
shape of an LSP `Position` under the default position encoding.

members.name: line
members.doc: 0-based line number.

members.name: character
members.doc: 0-based column in UTF-16 code units from the start of the line.

items.name: utf16Length
items.doc:
Returns the number of UTF-16 code units needed to encode `text`, with  
the same per-byte rule as `LineIndex` for bytes that are not UTF-8.

items.name: textUtf16UnitsBetween
items.signature: function textUtf16UnitsBetween(text: &String, start: u64, end: u64): u64
items.doc:
Counts the UTF-16 code units of the characters that lie entirely inside  
`start..end` of `text`. A character straddling `end` is not counted.

items.name: textUtf16UnitsOf
items.doc:
Number of UTF-16 code units for a sequence of `sequenceLength` UTF-8 bytes:  
two for a supplementary-plane character, one otherwise.

items.name: textUtf8SequenceLength
items.doc:
Returns the byte length of the well-formed UTF-8 sequence starting at  
`index`, or 1 when the byte there does not start one.  
  
Overlong encodings, surrogate code points and values above U+10FFFF are  
rejected with the same lead and second-byte ranges `str::from_utf8` uses,  
so every accepted sequence is one the host could have indexed.

items.name: checkedAddI64U64
items.signature: function checkedAddI64U64(base: i64, delta: u64): Option<i64>

items.name: checkedSubI64U64
items.signature: function checkedSubI64U64(base: i64, delta: u64): Option<i64>

items.name: checkedUnsignedDurationBetween
items.signature: function checkedUnsignedDurationBetween(leftSecs: u64, leftNanos: u32, rightSecs: u64, rightNanos: u32): Option<Duration>

items.name: compareUnsignedParts
items.signature: function compareUnsignedParts(leftSecs: u64, leftNanos: u32, rightSecs: u64, rightNanos: u32): i32

items.name: signedDifferenceToUnsigned
items.signature: function signedDifferenceToUnsigned(left: i64, right: i64): u64

items.name: Toml
items.doc:
Public TOML front-end for lexing, parsing, token inspection, and writing.  
  
Most users should call `Toml::parse` to obtain a `TomlDocument`. The lexer is  
exposed for tests and tooling that need token-level diagnostics or syntax  
highlighting.

items.name: lex
items.doc:
Lexes TOML source text from a borrowed string slice.  
  
This overload copies `source` into an owned `String` so the cursor and token  
construction paths can share the `&String` implementation.

items.name: lex
items.doc:
Lexes owned TOML source text into a fresh token vector.  
  
Whitespace except newlines is skipped, comments are ignored, CRLF and CR are  
normalized to newline tokens, and every successful token stream ends with  
`TomlTokenKind::EOF`.

items.name: lexInto
items.signature: function lexInto(source: str, tokens: &mut Vector<TomlToken>): Option<TomlError>
items.doc:
Lexes TOML source text into an existing token vector.  
  
The vector is cleared before tokens are appended. Returning `Option::NONE`  
means lexing succeeded and the vector ends with an EOF token.

items.name: lexInto
items.doc:
Lexes owned TOML source text into `tokens` without allocating a new vector.  
  
This is useful for callers that reuse token storage across parses. Existing  
contents are discarded before lexing starts. On error, the vector contains  
the tokens produced before the failing character or literal.

items.name: parse
items.doc:
Parses TOML source text from a borrowed string slice.  
  
This overload owns the text temporarily and delegates to `Toml::parse(&String)`.

items.name: parse
items.doc:
Parses owned TOML source text into a `TomlDocument`.  
  
Parsing is two-stage: source text is tokenized first, then `parseTokens`  
builds the table/value model. Lexer errors are returned unchanged; parser  
errors include duplicate keys, table conflicts, and unexpected tokens.

items.name: stringify
items.doc:
Rejects boolean TOML root serialization.  
  
TOML output currently supports record-like roots only; use a serializable  
record wrapper when emitting a document.

items.name: stringify
items.doc: Rejects character TOML root serialization.

items.name: stringify
items.doc: Rejects `i8` TOML root serialization.

items.name: stringify
items.doc: Rejects `i16` TOML root serialization.

items.name: stringify
items.doc: Rejects `i32` TOML root serialization.

items.name: stringify
items.doc: Rejects `i64` TOML root serialization.

items.name: stringify
items.doc: Rejects `u8` TOML root serialization.

items.name: stringify
items.doc: Rejects `u16` TOML root serialization.

items.name: stringify
items.doc: Rejects `u32` TOML root serialization.

items.name: stringify
items.doc: Rejects `u64` TOML root serialization.

items.name: stringify
items.doc: Rejects `f32` TOML root serialization.

items.name: stringify
items.doc: Rejects `f64` TOML root serialization.

items.name: stringify
items.doc: Rejects borrowed string TOML root serialization.

items.name: stringify
items.doc: Rejects owned string TOML root serialization.

items.name: stringify
items.doc:
Serializes a record-like value as a TOML document string.  
  
The type's `Serialize` implementation controls which fields are emitted.  
Serializer errors are propagated, including unsupported nested shapes or an  
implementation that does not produce a TOML-compatible root record.

items.name: tokenAt
items.doc: Returns the token at `index` when it exists.

items.name: tokenCount
items.doc:
Returns the number of tokens in a token vector.  
  
This small wrapper keeps token inspection available through the TOML module  
without exposing vector implementation details to simple tooling tests.

items.name: unsupportedRootValue
items.doc:
Returns the shared error for scalar TOML root serialization attempts.  
  
TOML documents require table-like roots. Primitive overloads of  
`stringify` route through this helper so they all report the same contract  
violation.

items.name: writer
items.doc:
Returns the serializer configuration used for TOML record output.  
  
The writer emits field entries as `key = value` lines, does not wrap records  
in braces, and rejects scalar roots.

members.name: slice
members.signature: slice(&self, startByte: u64, endByte: u64): String

items.name: TomlLexeme
items.doc:
Internal lexer result describing a token kind and its exclusive end offset.  
  
The lexer keeps decoded string contents separately in temporary `String`  
values. `TomlLexeme` records only the syntactic classification and how far  
the cursor advanced through the source text.

items.name: tomlAdvanceCount
items.signature: function tomlAdvanceCount(cursor: &mut TomlCursor, count: u64): void
items.doc: Advances the cursor by `count` UTF-8 characters.

items.name: tomlAscii
items.doc: Converts a decoded character to ASCII when TOML punctuation can use it.

items.name: tomlBooleanKind
items.doc: Classifies an identifier lexeme as a boolean keyword or a plain identifier.

items.name: tomlCharAtOrNull
items.doc:
Reads a character from `value`, returning `\0` when `index` is out of range.  
  
Number and date validators call this only on tokenizer candidate strings. The  
sentinel keeps validation branches explicit instead of relying on panics.

items.name: tomlCountDigits
items.doc: Counts consecutive decimal digits in `value` starting at `index`.

items.name: tomlHasLeadingZeroViolation
items.signature: function tomlHasLeadingZeroViolation(value: &String, start: u64, digitCount: u64): boolean
items.doc: Returns whether a multi-digit integer component starts with a forbidden `0`.

items.name: tomlHexValue
items.doc: Converts an ASCII hexadecimal digit into its numeric nibble value.

items.name: tomlIsBareKeyContinue
items.doc: Returns whether `ch` can continue an unquoted TOML bare key.

items.name: tomlIsBareKeyStart
items.doc: Returns whether `ch` can begin an unquoted TOML bare key.

items.name: tomlIsDateTimeMarker
items.doc: Returns whether `ch` suggests that a scalar literal may be date/time-shaped.

items.name: tomlIsDigit
items.doc: Returns whether `ch` is an ASCII decimal digit.

items.name: tomlIsExponentMarker
items.doc: Returns whether `ch` starts a floating-point exponent suffix.

items.name: tomlIsLiteralDelimiter
items.doc:
Returns whether `ch` terminates an unquoted scalar literal.  
  
Delimiters include whitespace, comments, collection separators, and key/value  
syntax. The scanned literal does not include the delimiter.

items.name: tomlIsSign
items.doc: Returns whether `ch` is a numeric sign accepted before numbers and offsets.

items.name: tomlLexBasicMultilineString
items.signature: function tomlLexBasicMultilineString(cursor: &mut TomlCursor, start: u64, output: &mut String): Result<TomlLexeme, TomlError>
items.doc:
Lexes a TOML basic multiline string (`"""..."""`).  
  
The decoded string contents are appended to `output`. Escapes are interpreted  
and the initial newline after the opening delimiter is trimmed according to  
TOML rules. Unterminated strings and invalid escapes return parser errors.

items.name: tomlLexBasicString
items.signature: function tomlLexBasicString(cursor: &mut TomlCursor, start: u64, output: &mut String): Result<TomlLexeme, TomlError>
items.doc:
Lexes a TOML basic string (`"..."`).  
  
Escapes are decoded into `output`. Bare newlines are rejected because ordinary  
basic strings cannot span lines.

items.name: tomlLexIdentifier
items.signature: function tomlLexIdentifier(cursor: &mut TomlCursor, start: u64): TomlLexeme
items.doc:
Lexes an identifier or bare-key token starting at `start`.  
  
The cursor is expected to be positioned at the first character of the key.  
It is advanced through all allowed continuation bytes and the returned  
lexeme stores the end offset for later slicing.

items.name: tomlLexInteger
items.signature: function tomlLexInteger(cursor: &mut TomlCursor, start: u64): Result<TomlLexeme, TomlError>
items.doc:
Lexes an integer or floating-point literal from a cursor position.  
  
This routine handles the fast path while walking the cursor. The stricter  
whole-literal validator is still used by `tomlLexScalarLiteral` for scanned  
scalar text; this helper exists for source positions known to begin with a  
sign or digit.

items.name: tomlLexLiteralString
items.signature: function tomlLexLiteralString(cursor: &mut TomlCursor, start: u64, output: &mut String): Result<TomlLexeme, TomlError>
items.doc:
Lexes a TOML literal or literal multiline string.  
  
Literal strings do not process escapes; source text between delimiters is  
copied directly into `output`. The multiline form trims one initial newline.

items.name: tomlLexQuotedString
items.signature: function tomlLexQuotedString(cursor: &mut TomlCursor, start: u64, output: &mut String): Result<TomlLexeme, TomlError>
items.doc: Dispatches to basic or basic multiline string lexing based on the delimiter.

items.name: tomlLexScalarLiteral
items.signature: function tomlLexScalarLiteral(cursor: &mut TomlCursor, start: u64): Result<TomlLexeme, TomlError>
items.doc:
Lexes a numeric or date/time scalar literal at `start`.  
  
Signed `inf` and `nan` are recognized before generic scanning. Date/time-like  
text is validated as a date/time token; all other scalar text is validated as  
an integer or float. Invalid candidates return precise TOML diagnostics.

items.name: tomlLexSignedFloatKeyword
items.doc:
Lexes signed special float keywords (`+inf`, `-inf`, `+nan`, `-nan`).  
  
On success the cursor is advanced past the keyword and a float lexeme is  
returned. Unsigned `inf` and `nan` are not handled here because this helper is  
only reached from sign-prefixed numeric paths.

items.name: tomlLooksLikeDateTime
items.doc:
Performs a cheap precheck for date/time-looking scalar text.  
  
This avoids routing ordinary integers through the stricter date/time  
validator while still recognizing local dates, local times, and offset forms.

items.name: tomlParseFixedDigits
items.signature: function tomlParseFixedDigits(value: &String, index: u64, digits: u64): i64
items.doc:
Parses exactly `digits` decimal digits at `index`, or returns `-1`.  
  
Date/time validation uses the sentinel to validate fixed-width components  
without allocating substrings.

items.name: tomlPeekAscii
items.doc: Peeks at the cursor and returns the current character only when it is ASCII.

items.name: tomlPushEscaped
items.signature: function tomlPushEscaped(value: &mut String, escaped: char): boolean
items.doc:
Appends the decoded value for a basic-string single-character escape.  
  
Returns `false` when `escaped` is not one of TOML's recognized short escape  
codes. Unicode escapes are handled by `tomlPushQuotedEscape`.

items.name: tomlPushIdentifierToken
items.signature: function tomlPushIdentifierToken(tokens: &mut Vector<TomlToken>, cursor: &mut TomlCursor, start: u64): void
items.doc: Lexes and pushes a bare identifier or boolean token.

items.name: tomlPushIntegerToken
items.signature: function tomlPushIntegerToken(tokens: &mut Vector<TomlToken>, cursor: &mut TomlCursor, start: u64): Result<boolean, TomlError>
items.doc: Lexes and pushes a numeric or date/time scalar token.

items.name: tomlPushLiteralStringToken
items.signature: function tomlPushLiteralStringToken(tokens: &mut Vector<TomlToken>, cursor: &mut TomlCursor, start: u64): Result<boolean, TomlError>
items.doc: Lexes and pushes a decoded literal string token.

items.name: tomlPushLiteralToken
items.signature: function tomlPushLiteralToken(tokens: &mut Vector<TomlToken>, kind: TomlTokenKind, lexeme: str, span: TomlSpan): void
items.doc: Pushes a token whose lexeme is a static string slice.

items.name: tomlPushQuotedEscape
items.signature: function tomlPushQuotedEscape(output: &mut String, cursor: &mut TomlCursor, escapedStart: u64, escapedAscii: char): Result<boolean, TomlError>
items.doc:
Decodes one escape sequence in a basic string or basic multiline string.  
  
The cursor is positioned at the escaped character, not at the preceding  
backslash. Short escapes and Unicode scalar escapes are appended to `output`;  
invalid escapes return `TomlError::InvalidEscape`.

items.name: tomlPushQuotedToken
items.signature: function tomlPushQuotedToken(tokens: &mut Vector<TomlToken>, cursor: &mut TomlCursor, start: u64): Result<boolean, TomlError>
items.doc: Lexes and pushes a decoded basic string token.

items.name: tomlPushStringToken
items.signature: function tomlPushStringToken(tokens: &mut Vector<TomlToken>, kind: TomlTokenKind, lexeme: &String, span: TomlSpan): void
items.doc: Pushes a token by cloning an owned string lexeme into the token vector.

items.name: tomlPushUtf8Scalar
items.signature: function tomlPushUtf8Scalar(output: &mut String, scalar: u32): boolean
items.doc:
Encodes a Unicode scalar value into `output` as UTF-8 bytes.  
  
Returns `false` for surrogate code points and values above the Unicode scalar  
range. The implementation writes encoded bytes explicitly so UTF-8 byte  
boundaries stay stable even though `String::pushChar` now accepts scalars.

items.name: tomlReadHexScalar
items.signature: function tomlReadHexScalar(cursor: &mut TomlCursor, start: u64, digits: u64): Result<u32, TomlError>
items.doc:
Reads a fixed-width hexadecimal Unicode scalar from the cursor.  
  
The cursor is advanced over exactly `digits` hex characters on success. Any  
missing, non-ASCII, or non-hex character returns an invalid-escape error at  
the offending source span.

items.name: tomlRemainingStartsWith
items.signature: function tomlRemainingStartsWith(cursor: &mut TomlCursor, expected: str): boolean
items.doc:
Returns whether the cursor's remaining source starts with `expected`.  
  
The cursor position is not changed. This helper is used for multi-character  
delimiters such as triple-quoted strings and signed float keywords.

items.name: tomlScanLiteralEnd
items.doc:
Advances through an unquoted scalar literal and returns its end offset.  
  
Scanning stops at the first literal delimiter, non-ASCII character, or end of  
input. The cursor is left at the returned offset.

items.name: tomlSkipComment
items.doc:
Advances `cursor` over a TOML comment without consuming the line ending.  
  
The caller handles newlines as significant top-level separators, so this  
helper stops immediately before `\n` or `\r`.

items.name: tomlTrimInitialMultilineNewline
items.doc:
Consumes the optional first newline after a multiline string opening marker.  
  
TOML trims one immediately following line ending for both basic and literal  
multiline strings. CRLF is consumed as a single logical newline.

items.name: tomlValidateDateTimeLiteral
items.doc:
Validates TOML local-date, local-time, local-date-time, and offset literals.  
  
The tokenizer stores the original text as the value lexeme; this function  
only decides whether the candidate is structurally valid enough to become a  
date/time token.

items.name: tomlValidateNumberLiteral
items.doc:
Validates a TOML numeric literal and returns its token kind.  
  
Valid integers return `TomlTokenKind::INTEGER`; valid floats return  
`TomlTokenKind::FLOAT`. `TomlTokenKind::EOF` is used as an internal invalid  
sentinel so callers can choose the appropriate diagnostic span.

items.name: tomlValidateTimeTail
items.doc:
Validates the time, fractional second, and optional offset tail of a literal.  
  
`index` must point to the first hour digit. The accepted forms are local time  
(`HH:MM:SS` with optional fraction), `Z` offsets, and signed `+HH:MM` or  
`-HH:MM` offsets.

items.name: TomlError
items.doc: Structured TOML error with source span information.

members.name: kind
members.doc: Stable error category for matching in caller code.

members.name: message
members.doc: Human-readable diagnostic message.

members.name: span
members.doc: Byte span in the original TOML input associated with the failure.

members.name: duplicateKey
members.doc: Creates a duplicate-key parser error.

members.name: invalidDateTime
members.doc: Creates an invalid date or datetime lexer error.

members.name: invalidEscape
members.doc: Creates an invalid string escape error.

members.name: invalidInteger
members.doc: Creates an invalid-integer lexer error.

members.name: invalidNumber
members.doc: Creates an invalid-number lexer error.

members.name: lookupNotFound
members.doc: Creates a lookup-not-found access error.

members.name: lookupTypeMismatch
members.doc: Creates a lookup type-mismatch access error.

members.name: new
members.signature: static new(kind: TomlErrorKind, message: str, span: TomlSpan): TomlError
members.doc: Creates a TOML error from an explicit kind, message, and span.

members.name: tableConflict
members.doc: Creates a table-conflict parser error.

members.name: unexpectedCharacter
members.doc: Creates an unexpected-character lexer error.

members.name: unexpectedToken
members.doc: Creates an unexpected-token parser error.

members.name: unterminatedString
members.doc: Creates an unterminated-string lexer error.

members.name: clone
members.doc: Returns a shallow clone of the error.

items.name: TomlErrorKind
items.doc: Machine-readable TOML parse or lookup failure category.

items.name: parseTokens
items.doc:
Parses a complete token stream into a `TomlDocument`.  
  
The stream is expected to come from the TOML tokenizer and normally ends with  
an EOF token. The parser accepts top-level key/value assignments, explicit  
table headers (`[table]`), and arrays of tables (`[[table]]`). On success it  
returns a fully owned document rooted at an explicit table; on failure it  
returns the first syntax, duplicate-key, or table-conflict error encountered.

items.name: tomlAppendArrayTableHeader
items.signature: function tomlAppendArrayTableHeader(rootPointer: *mut TomlTable, segments: &Vector<String>, lastSpan: TomlSpan, headerSpan: TomlSpan): Result<*mut TomlTable, TomlError>
items.doc:
Opens an `[[array-of-tables]]` header and returns the appended table pointer.  
  
Missing prefix tables are created implicitly. If the final key already holds  
an array of tables, a new explicit table is appended and becomes current. If  
the final key holds any other value kind, parsing fails with a table  
conflict.

items.name: tomlCombineSpan
items.signature: function tomlCombineSpan(start: TomlSpan, end: TomlSpan): TomlSpan
items.doc:
Builds a span covering the source range from `start.start` to `end.end`.  
  
Callers pass the first and last token spans of a syntactic construct, such as  
an array, table header, or dotted key.

items.name: tomlDateTimeKind
items.doc:
Classifies a tokenized TOML date/time lexeme by its visible separators.  
  
Date/time component decoding is intentionally deferred; `TomlDateTime` keeps  
the original text and this kind enum. The classifier distinguishes offset  
date-times, local date-times, local times, and local dates using TOML's  
separators after the lexer has accepted the literal.

items.name: tomlEnsurePrefixTable
items.signature: function tomlEnsurePrefixTable(tablePointer: *mut TomlTable, segment: &String, segmentSpan: TomlSpan, conflictSpan: TomlSpan, createState: TomlTableState, allowInlineDescend: boolean): Result<*mut TomlTable, TomlError>
items.doc:
Returns or creates the table reached by a prefix path segment.  
  
Prefixes in dotted keys and headers must resolve to tables, or to the latest  
element of an array-of-tables. Missing prefixes are created with  
`createState`. Inline tables are closed values in normal document parsing,  
but inline-table parsing can set `allowInlineDescend` to permit dotted keys  
inside the same inline table expression.

items.name: tomlExpectLineEnd
items.signature: function tomlExpectLineEnd(tokens: &Vector<TomlToken>, index: u64): Result<u64, TomlError>
items.doc:
Requires the next token to terminate a top-level TOML item.  
  
A valid terminator is a newline sequence or EOF. On success the returned  
index points to the first token after any consumed newlines, or to the EOF  
token itself. Any other token means the current key/value or table header has  
trailing syntax and is reported as `UnexpectedToken`.

items.name: tomlInsertValueAtPath
items.signature: function tomlInsertValueAtPath(tablePointer: *mut TomlTable, segments: &Vector<String>, lastSpan: TomlSpan, value: TomlValue, conflictSpan: TomlSpan, allowInlineDescend: boolean): Option<TomlError>
items.doc:
Inserts a parsed value into `tablePointer` at a dotted key path.  
  
Intermediate path segments are resolved through `tomlEnsurePrefixTable`.  
Existing scalar values at the final segment produce `DuplicateKey`; existing  
tables or arrays of tables at the final segment produce `TableConflict`.  
Returning `Option::NONE` means the value was inserted successfully.

items.name: tomlLastSpan
items.doc:
Returns the span of the final token in a token stream.  
  
The parser uses this as a fallback diagnostic location when it reaches the  
end of the stream while still expecting a token. Empty streams map to the  
zero-width span `0..0`, which keeps parser helpers total even when called on  
malformed or manually constructed token vectors.

items.name: tomlOpenTableHeader
items.signature: function tomlOpenTableHeader(rootPointer: *mut TomlTable, segments: &Vector<String>, lastSpan: TomlSpan, headerSpan: TomlSpan): Result<*mut TomlTable, TomlError>
items.doc:
Opens an explicit `[table]` header and returns the active table pointer.  
  
Missing prefix tables are created implicitly. The final table may be newly  
created or may be an implicit table promoted to explicit. Re-opening an  
explicit table, targeting a scalar, or targeting an array of tables is a TOML  
table conflict.

items.name: tomlParseArray
items.signature: function tomlParseArray(tokens: &Vector<TomlToken>, index: u64, keySpan: TomlSpan, output: &mut TomlValue): Result<u64, TomlError>
items.doc:
Parses a TOML array value starting at `[`.  
  
Arrays may contain nested arrays and inline tables. Newlines are accepted  
after `[` and after commas, and a trailing comma before `]` is accepted. The  
parser preserves element order and stores an aggregate span from the opening  
bracket through the closing bracket.

items.name: tomlParseBooleanLiteral
items.doc:
Converts a tokenized TOML boolean lexeme into a boolean value.  
  
The lexer only emits boolean tokens for valid `true` and `false` literals, so  
the parser can distinguish them by length and first byte.

items.name: tomlParseInlineTable
items.signature: function tomlParseInlineTable(tokens: &Vector<TomlToken>, index: u64, keySpan: TomlSpan, output: &mut TomlValue): Result<u64, TomlError>
items.doc:
Parses a TOML inline table value starting at `{`.  
  
Inline table entries use the same dotted-key insertion logic as top-level  
assignments, but `allowInlineDescend` is enabled so dotted keys can construct  
nested tables within the inline value. The resulting table state is marked  
`INLINE`, which prevents later document-level headers from extending it.

items.name: tomlParseIntegerLiteral
items.doc:
Converts a tokenized TOML integer lexeme into an `i64`.  
  
The tokenizer is responsible for validating the grammar. This routine only  
applies the optional sign and ignores `_` separators while accumulating base  
10 digits. It does not perform overflow checking.

items.name: tomlParsePath
items.signature: function tomlParsePath(tokens: &Vector<TomlToken>, index: u64, segments: &mut Vector<String>, firstSpan: &mut TomlSpan, lastSpan: &mut TomlSpan): Result<u64, TomlError>
items.doc:
Parses a dotted TOML key path into `segments`.  
  
The path starts at `index` and accepts bare identifiers and quoted string  
keys separated by dots. Parsed segment text is appended to `segments`,  
`firstSpan` is updated to the first segment, and `lastSpan` is updated after  
each segment. The returned index points to the first token after the path.

items.name: tomlParseScalarValue
items.signature: function tomlParseScalarValue(token: &TomlToken, keySpan: TomlSpan): Result<TomlValue, TomlError>
items.doc:
Converts a scalar token into an owned `TomlValue`.  
  
Supported scalar tokens are strings, integers, floats, booleans, and  
date/time literals. Array and inline-table tokens are handled by their own  
recursive parsers. `keySpan` is recorded on the created value so duplicate-key  
and lookup diagnostics can point back to the key that introduced it.

items.name: tomlParseValue
items.signature: function tomlParseValue(tokens: &Vector<TomlToken>, index: u64, keySpan: TomlSpan, output: &mut TomlValue): Result<u64, TomlError>
items.doc:
Parses any TOML value at `index` into `output`.  
  
Arrays and inline tables are parsed recursively. Scalar values are converted  
directly from the current token. The returned index points to the first token  
after the value, leaving separators and line terminators for the caller.

items.name: tomlParserCharAtOrNull
items.doc:
Reads a character from `value`, returning `\0` when `index` is out of range.  
  
Literal parsing in this file is only called after tokenization has already  
validated the token shape. The sentinel keeps the small classification  
helpers simple without turning tokenizer invariants into parser panics.

items.name: tomlSkipNewlines
items.doc:
Advances past consecutive newline tokens starting at `index`.  
  
TOML allows newlines between array elements and between top-level entries.  
The returned index is either the first non-newline token or the stream end.

items.name: tomlTokenAt
items.signature: function tomlTokenAt(tokens: &Vector<TomlToken>, index: u64): Result<&TomlToken, TomlError>
items.doc:
Returns the token at `index`, or an unexpected-token error at the stream end.  
  
This helper centralizes bounds handling for the recursive-descent parser so  
individual parsing routines can report the last known span instead of  
relying on unchecked vector access.

items.name: TomlSpan
items.doc:
Byte span into the original TOML source text.  
  
Spans are half-open byte ranges: `start` is inclusive and `end` is exclusive.  
They intentionally use byte offsets so diagnostics can point into UTF-8 input  
without depending on display width or terminal rendering.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
let span: TomlSpan = TomlSpan::new(4, 12);  
```

members.name: start
members.doc: Inclusive byte offset where the span begins.

members.name: end
members.doc: Exclusive byte offset where the span ends.

members.name: new
members.signature: static new(start: u64, end: u64): TomlSpan
members.doc:
Creates a new source span from byte offsets.  
  
The constructor does not validate ordering. Lexer and parser code should  
pass stable offsets from the original source cursor.  
  
# Arguments  
  
- `start`: inclusive byte offset.  
- `end`: exclusive byte offset.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
let empty: TomlSpan = TomlSpan::new(0, 0);  
let key: TomlSpan = TomlSpan::new(0, 7);  
```

items.name: TomlToken
items.doc:
Owned TOML token with original source span.  
  
Tokens own their lexeme text. This keeps parser cursors valid after lexer  
helper strings go out of scope and makes snapshots deterministic.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
let token: TomlToken = TomlToken::new(  
  TomlTokenKind::IDENTIFIER,  
  "package",  
  TomlSpan::new(0, 7),  
);  
```

members.name: kind
members.doc: Token category.

members.name: lexeme
members.doc: Owned token text after lexer normalization.

members.name: span
members.doc: Byte span in the original input.

members.name: create
members.signature: static create(kind: TomlTokenKind, lexeme: &String, span: TomlSpan): TomlToken
members.doc:
Creates a token by cloning a referenced `String` value.  
  
Use this overload when parser or lexer code only has a borrowed reference  
but the token must retain independent storage.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
let text: String = String::create("value");  
let token: TomlToken = TomlToken::create(TomlTokenKind::STRING, &text, TomlSpan::new(1, 8));  
```

members.name: create
members.signature: static create(kind: TomlTokenKind, lexeme: String, span: TomlSpan): TomlToken
members.doc:
Creates a token by cloning an owned `String` value.  
  
Use this overload when lexer code built a `String` while decoding escapes.  
The caller keeps ownership of the original string.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
let text: String = String::create("value");  
let token: TomlToken = TomlToken::create(TomlTokenKind::STRING, text, TomlSpan::new(1, 8));  
```

members.name: new
members.signature: static new(kind: TomlTokenKind, lexeme: str, span: TomlSpan): TomlToken
members.doc:
Creates a token by copying a borrowed string slice into owned storage.  
  
# Arguments  
  
- `kind`: token category.  
- `lexeme`: borrowed token text to copy.  
- `span`: source byte span.  
  
# Example  
  

items.name: TomlParserCursor
items.doc:
Cursor over a TOML token stream used by parser tests and parser helpers.  
  
The cursor is a lightweight view into a `Vector<TomlToken>`. It does not own  
the token memory; callers must keep the source vector alive while the cursor  
is used.  
  
# Cursor Model  
  
```text  
  tokens:  [IDENTIFIER][EQUALS][STRING][EOF]  
            index=0  
  
  advance() -> IDENTIFIER, index=1  
  peekKind() -> EQUALS, index stays 1  
```

members.name: tokens
members.doc: Borrowed pointer to token storage owned by a `Vector<TomlToken>`.

members.name: length
members.doc: Number of tokens available through `tokens`.

members.name: index
members.doc: Current cursor index.

members.name: create
members.doc:
Creates a cursor over a token vector.  
  
# Arguments  
  
- `tokens`: token vector to view. It must outlive the cursor.  
  
# Returns  
  
A cursor positioned at index 0.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
let cursor: TomlParserCursor = TomlParserCursor::create(&tokens);  
```

members.name: advance
members.doc:
Consumes the current token and returns its kind.  
  
If the cursor is already past the stream, the index is unchanged and the  
result is `Option::NONE`.

members.signature: expect(&mut self, kind: TomlTokenKind): Result<TomlSpan, TomlError>
members.doc:
Requires the current token to have a specific kind and consumes it.  
  
# Returns  
  
`Result::OK(span)` with the consumed token span on success, or  
`Result::ERROR(TomlError::unexpectedToken(...))` when the stream is empty  
or the current token has a different kind.

members.name: isAtEnd
members.doc:
Returns whether the cursor is positioned at the logical end of input.  
  
A missing token or an explicit `EOF` token both count as end-of-input.

members.name: matchKind
members.doc:
Consumes the current token only if it has the requested kind.

`true` when a token was consumed, otherwise `false`.

members.name: peekKind
members.doc:
Returns the kind of the current token without advancing.  
  
Returns `Option::NONE` when the cursor has no token storage or has moved  
past the end of the token stream.

members.name: peekLexeme
members.doc:
Returns the current token lexeme without advancing.  
  
The returned `str` borrows from the token's owned `String`. It remains valid  
as long as the underlying token vector is alive.

members.name: peekSpan
members.doc:
Returns the current token span without advancing.  
  
Use this for diagnostics that need to report the lookahead token.

members.name: previousSpan
members.doc:
Returns the span of the previously consumed token.  
  
At the beginning of the stream there is no previous token, so this returns  
an empty zero span.

members.name: skipNewlines
members.doc:
Consumes consecutive `NEWLINE` tokens.  
  
TOML parsing uses newlines as statement separators. This helper centralizes  
the common pattern of allowing blank lines between table headers and  
assignments.

members.name: tokenSpan
members.doc:
Returns a diagnostic span for the current cursor position.  
  
If the cursor is at EOF or past the end, the last token span is used as a  
fallback so errors still point near the source location that ended parsing.

items.signature: function tomlLookupInTable(table: &TomlTable, segments: &Vector<String>, index: u64, fallbackSpan: TomlSpan): Result<TomlValue, TomlError>

Recursively resolves dotted path segments inside a TOML table.  
  
# Arguments  
  
- `table`: current table to inspect.  
- `segments`: split path segments.  
- `index`: current segment index.

items.name: tomlOwnedStr
items.doc:
Copies a borrowed string into TOML-owned string storage.  
  
TOML values store string-like payloads as `str` for compact access, but the  
backing memory must outlive parser temporaries. This overload first creates  
an owned `String`, then delegates to the `&String` overload that allocates a  
NUL-terminated byte buffer.  
  
# Arguments  
  
- `value`: borrowed UTF-8 string slice to preserve.  
  
# Returns  
  
A `str` pointing to newly allocated TOML-owned storage.  
  
# Example  
  
```ignis  
let owned: str = tomlOwnedStr("package");  
```

items.name: tomlOwnedStr
items.doc:
Copies a `String` into TOML-owned NUL-terminated storage.  
  
This helper is used by tokens, values, and table entries that need to store a  
stable `str` after parser-local `String` values go out of scope. The memory is  
allocated with `Memory::allocateVector<u8>` and is intentionally not reclaimed  
by the TOML value model yet.  
  
# Arguments  
  
- `value`: owned string whose bytes should be copied.  
  
# Returns  
  
A `str` view into newly allocated storage with a trailing NUL byte.  
  
# Memory Layout  
  
```text  
  input bytes: [p][k][g]  
  allocated:   [p][k][g][\0]  
                        ▲  
                        C-string terminator for str interop  
```

items.name: tomlPathSegments

Splits a dotted TOML lookup path into owned string segments.  
  
Lookup helpers use this for public `"a.b.c"` path APIs. It performs a simple  
byte split on `.` and does not implement quoted-key escaping; callers that  
need exact TOML syntax should use parsed document paths instead.

items.name: tomlUnexpectedParserSpan
items.signature: function tomlUnexpectedParserSpan(tokens: *mut TomlToken, length: u64, index: u64): TomlSpan
items.doc:
Returns the best diagnostic span for a parser cursor position.  
  
Parser cursors may point at EOF or one position past the last real token.  
This helper keeps error reporting stable by using the requested token span  
when available, or the last token span as a fallback.  
  
# Arguments  
  
- `tokens`: pointer to the first token in the stream.  
- `length`: number of tokens in the stream.  
- `index`: cursor index that triggered an error.  
  
# Returns  
  
A stable span for diagnostics. Empty streams return `TomlSpan::new(0, 0)`.
